s: A company has 45 VPCs in 30 AWS accounts in us-east-1. All accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations, and new accounts are added every month. The company has a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection from its data center. Every VPC must reach on-premises networks privately, VPCs must be able to communicate with each other, and on-premises connectivity must fail over automatically to an encrypted path over the internet if the Direct Connect connection fails. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Create a transit gateway in a network account and share it with the organization by using AWS RAM. Attach every VPC. Create a Direct Connect gateway, create a transit VIF on the connection to the Direct Connect gateway, and associate the Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway. Create a Site-to-Site VPN attachment on the transit gateway as the backup path.

Create a private VIF for each VPC on the Direct Connect connection that terminates on a virtual private gateway in that VPC. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection from each virtual private gateway as the backup. Use VPC peering for VPC-to-VPC traffic.

Create a transit gateway and share it with the organization by using AWS RAM. Attach every VPC. Create a transit VIF on the Direct Connect connection and attach the VIF directly to the transit gateway. Create a Site-to-Site VPN attachment on the transit gateway as the backup path.
Create a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection and run a Site-to-Site VPN over it to a transit gateway shared by AWS RAM. Create a second Site-to-Site VPN over the internet as the backup path.

w.y: One transit gateway shared through AWS RAM gives every current and future account transitive VPC-to-VPC and hybrid routing, and a single transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway associated with the transit gateway carries all VPC prefixes. A VPN attachment on the same transit gateway provides automatic BGP failover because the transit gateway prefers Direct Connect gateway routes over VPN routes for the same prefix, which is the LEAST operational overhead.

o.A: Correct: shared transit gateway + transit VIF/DX gateway + VPN attachment gives scalable, transitive routing with automatic failover.
o.B: Per-VPC VIFs, per-VPC VPNs and a peering mesh must be rebuilt for every new account; this is the highest overhead and does not scale.
o.C: A transit VIF cannot attach directly to a transit gateway; it must terminate on a Direct Connect gateway that is associated with the transit gateway.
o.D: VPN over a public VIF works but caps throughput at about 1.25 Gbps per tunnel and adds tunnel management; encryption over DX was not required.
